outcomes.description: Paper is stuffed into the cup.
outcomes.target: The paper is visibly placed inside the cup, with evidence that it has been stuffed into it rather than merely resting nearby or on its rim.
outcomes.reference: The requested edit is stated in the instruction: “Stuffing the paper into the cup”.

nodes.question: Can the paper and potential receiving objects be inventoried, and what concrete source-to-edit features support, contradict, or leave unresolved the edited object's identity as a cup?
nodes.criteria: Pass if visibility permits a grounded inventory of the paper and relevant receiving-object region, even if cup identity is disproved or unresolved. Report paper identity and cup identity separately as established, disproved, or unresolved, with decisive features and visibility limits. Describe the paper's visible boundaries and overlap without awarding insertion credit. Fail if adequate visibility positively establishes absence of the paper or any relevant receiving object. Unknown if visibility prevents a grounded inventory. A visible non-cup is usable negative identity evidence, not automatically an inventory failure; failure to see an interior alone does not disprove a cup.
nodes.binding: Inspect both images directly. Locate the source's blue cup, its broad opening and wall geometry, and the source paper; compare these structures with the edited paper and exposed reddish object. Correspondence in position or overlap does not preserve object identity, and a color change alone does not disprove it. Examine whether the reddish contour and dark marking jointly describe a receiving vessel, a closed rounded object, or an ambiguous structure. Treat a ball-like contour and seam as a hypothesis to test, not a supplied fact. Explain which visible features favor each interpretation. Record which paper edges remain visible, whether any disappear behind a receiving boundary, and whether another relevant cup is visible. If uncertainty is attributed to occlusion, identify the specific hidden feature needed to decide; do not treat every covered surface as decisive. Do not infer stuffing from the hand's grip.

nodes.question: Within s1's inventoried scene, does independent source-and-edit inspection establish paper insertion or intermediate stuffing into a cup, establish no requested progress, or leave a specific necessary relation unresolved?
nodes.criteria: Pass if concrete visible features establish paper and a receiving cup and show paper entering or occupying its interior, or crossing its opening with deformation sufficient to establish intermediate stuffing. State the entry cues and whether they indicate intermediate or potentially completed progress; this check alone does not establish completion. Fail if adequate visibility positively establishes no requested progress: paper wholly external to a cup without entry or stuffing, demonstrably rim-only placement without insertion, or absence of a required receiving cup. A positively identified non-cup supports fail only when visible paper placement and the relevant receiving region also exclude insertion into another cup. Report these negative findings separately. Unknown if a specific unresolved identity, paper boundary, or occlusion materially prevents distinguishing actual entry from external overlap. Neither absence of a visible opening alone nor speculative hidden geometry establishes fail or unknown.
nodes.binding: Use s1 as coarse ancestor context, retaining its observations but independently reassessing its identity conclusion. Compare the source cup's opening and enclosing walls with the edited object's exposed contour and dark marking. Determine whether the marking is supported as an opening boundary, surface seam, or unresolved feature; test vessel and closed-object interpretations without assuming either. Trace visible paper edges and their occlusion order relative to the reddish boundary. Distinguish an edge continuing in front of an external surface from an edge entering behind a receiving rim or wall. Inspect the relevant scene for another receiving cup. For a negative finding, cite incompatible object features and affirmative external-placement or absence evidence, explaining why the covered region does not leave a materially plausible insertion alternative. For unknown, identify the actual decisive hidden boundary or identity feature and why visible structure cannot resolve it. Missing entry cues alone are insufficient negative evidence. Do not inherit s1's uncertainty automatically, infer motion from a grip, or count object replacement and unrelated changes as requested progress.

nodes.question: Given the visual inventory and direct opening-entry investigation, does the edited image establish completed stuffing of the paper into a cup?
nodes.criteria: Pass if concrete evidence identifies paper and a cup and shows the paper extending inside it with visible containment, compression, or insertion sufficient to establish stuffing. Fail if adequate visual evidence positively establishes the full target is not met, including incomplete insertion, wholly external paper, rim-only placement, or adequately visible absence of a required object. Report whether failure coexists with actual insertion progress or with no progress, without treating completion failure as proof of either. Unknown if identity, containment, or the distinction between completed stuffing and an intermediate state remains unresolved. Some paper may remain outside a successfully stuffed cup.
nodes.binding: Use s1 and s4_opening_entry as ancestor context, then inspect the edited image directly for completed stuffing. Do not treat s1's inventory pass as confirmed cup identity or s4's progress pass as completion. Cite the decisive containment or compression cues and reconcile any disagreement with ancestor observations using visible evidence. Do not infer an interior hidden behind the sheet, require preservation of the source cup's color, or count unrelated changes as progress.

nodes.question: Does the image show the paper stuffed inside the cup?
nodes.criteria: Use all and only s1, s4_opening_entry, and s2 observations in that order. s1 provides inventory and identity context, never completion credit. Complete requires grounded paper-and-cup identity, actual insertion evidence from s4_opening_entry, and affirmative completed stuffing evidence from s2. Partial requires positively established insertion or intermediate stuffing from s4_opening_entry and positively established incompleteness from s2. Absent requires affirmative no-progress evidence from s4_opening_entry: trustworthy wholly external or rim-only placement without insertion, or adequately established absence of a required receiving cup. Identification of the reddish candidate as a non-cup alone is insufficient unless the saved evidence also excludes another relevant receiving cup or insertion. s2 failure alone never establishes absent. An earlier unresolved identity can be resolved by a later support's independent concrete evidence; an adequately resolved negative does not require affirmative cup identity. Unknown applies when evidence necessary for the proposed classification remains unresolved or contradictory without a grounded reconciliation. Do not promote lack of visible entry into proof of absence, supporting passes into completion, or dependent observations into independent confirmation. Infer no new visual facts.

program.checker_template:
Execute ONE saved check. Return status, evidence, confidence (0 to 1 or null), and used_dependency_ids. You receive no reference label or optimizer feedback. Do not predict what the optimizer wants.
Support checks receive source and edited images. Inspect only the saved visual proposition and binding. When dependencies are supplied, use those ancestor observations as context and investigate the more specific proposition yourself; do not simply repeat the parent answer. Use pass/fail/unknown. A pass on a broad parent does not imply a nested check passes. Known negative evidence is usable; uncertain or missing evidence is unknown. Do not award requested completion credit to supporting facts.
The requested fulfillment readout receives NO images. Use ALL and ONLY saved support observations, the original instruction, rubric and saved composition criteria. Use complete/partial/absent/unknown. Mere texture or object presence must not silently establish whole-image conversion or a requested spatial relation. Known progress plus evidenced incompleteness may be partial; absence means no requested progress. Missing necessary evidence is unknown, never a fabricated failure or completion. Do not infer new visual facts.
used_dependency_ids must name every supplied dependency check_id exactly once in saved order (empty when none). Confidence is self-report, not calibrated correctness.
